statements.text: Small claims court shares original jurisdiction with county and district courts over covered civil claims for debt, damages or the value of personal property up to $7,500, excluding interest and costs, with civil penalties included where provided by law.
The clerk of the small claims court makes all necessary small claims forms available.
A small claims action begins on a prescribed complaint form. The C.R.C.P. 500 series governs filing and service of that form.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rules 500 series

statements.text: The 2024 statute sets the small claims plaintiff's docket fee at $31 for a money judgment of $500 or less and $55 for a money judgment above $500 through $7,500.
C.R.S. § 13-32-101(1)(c)(IV) governs the current small claims docket fees.
The small claims court holds hearings at times set by the judge or magistrate or ordered by the supreme court.
The estimated wait for a small claims hearing is 30 to 60 days (C.R.S. § 13-6-406 governs hearing scheduling).

The judge or magistrate conducts the small claims trial to do justice between the parties. Formal procedural and pleading requirements and technical evidence rules do not bind the trial, except as provided by supreme court rules for small claims.

Individuals generally represent themselves in small claims. Attorney participation is restricted, with statutory exceptions and exceptions permitted by supreme court rule. If an attorney appears as allowed under subsection (2) or (3), the other parties may be represented by counsel.
Discovery in small claims court is limited or unavailable under the C.R.C.P. 500 series.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rules 500 series

statements.text: There is no right to jury trial in small claims court.
Either party may appeal under the county court rules. On appeal, the laws and rules for county court appeals govern, including the right to counsel.
The C.R.C.P. 300 series governs the scope of small claims appeals, including whether review is limited to procedural errors.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rules 300 series

statements.text: Small claims jurisdiction includes qualifying contract actions for specific performance, disaffirmance, avoidance or rescission up to $7,500. Injunctive relief falls outside small claims jurisdiction except for the matters specified in subsection (2)(h).
A counterclaim above the small claims court's jurisdiction is removed to the county or district court of appropriate jurisdiction under supreme court rules.
